real_estate.homebuilder: About 4 in 10 Alameda County homeowners 75 and older still carry a mortgage, against 28.7% nationally.
real_estate.commentary:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average was 7.51% at Monday's update, with the 15-year at 7.04%; Tuesday's reading had not posted by 8:56 AM PT. On today's $1,275,000 Fremont median with 20% down, that is about $7,139 a month in principal and interest.

More homeowners are still paying off a mortgage late in life. In 2025, 28.7% of U.S. homeowners 75 and older still had one, up from 20.3% in 2010, and their number more than doubled to about 3.9 million, according to Census Bureau survey data (chart). Here the share is higher: 41.5% of Alameda County homeowners 75 and older carry a mortgage, about 19,600 households, up from 27.3% in 2010 and above California's 39.1%. If more of those owners stay put, fewer homes come up for resale.

Tuesday's export shows 2,381 board wide, from 2,408 Monday, with 132 coming soon and 136 brand new. The five city ledger is 604, from 606: Hayward (176) added one, Milpitas (96) fell two and Newark (70) one, while Fremont (205) and Union City (57) held. The five city median list price crossed a million, to $1,024,950 from $999,988.

What this means for you: sellers, an existing loan is not a reason to hold off, since it is paid off at closing. Buyers, resale supply stays thin when owners stay put, so be preapproved before the right home lists.

• Board wide: 2,381 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 132 coming soon and 136 brand new.

📍 Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

• Live ledger: 604 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 539 are on the market and 65 are coming soon.
• Fremont: 205 live, 166 active, 24 coming soon and 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,275,000 at $787 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 39 days.
• The rest of the ledger: Hayward 176, Milpitas 96, Newark 70, Union City 57.
• Across all five cities the median is $1,024,950 at $666 a square foot. 268 homes are priced under a million, and 191 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

feature_image.alt: Donut charts: 20.3% of U.S. homeowners 75 and older had a mortgage in 2010 (1.79 million) and 28.7% in 2025 (3.93 million), 2.2 times as many. Local panel: in Alameda County the share rose from 27.3% (about 8,200 homeowners) to 41.5% (about 19,600), against 39.1% in California.
feature_image.caption: More homeowners 75 and older still have a mortgage, and Alameda County runs well above the nation.
feature_image.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 1-year estimates, table B25027, 2010 and 2025

economy.note: Closing levels for Monday, November 16: the 10-Year is Treasury's daily close, gold and silver are December COMEX settlements, and Brent is the ICE January settlement. Live moves at 8:56 AM PT are in the commentary.
economy.commentary:
Diesel slipped under $6 a gallon. The U.S. average was $5.94 in the Energy Information Administration's Nov. 16 survey, the first week under $6 since early September and down from the $6.53 record on Sept. 21 (chart). California is at $7.73, about $1.80 above the national average and off its own $8.25 record that week. Diesel is still up about 53% from a year ago, and it moves the trucks behind groceries and building materials alike, so a lasting slide would ease prices down the line.

The 10-Year Treasury yield closed Monday at 5.12%, down from 5.15% Friday; Market Briefs printed it up at 5.13%. Gold settled at $3,853.00 and silver at $46.86, and both are firmer this morning: gold near $3,868.30 (+0.40%) and silver near $47.46 (+1.28%). Brent settled at $92.44, down 3.55%, not the $91.68 Market Briefs printed, and is near $93.27 this morning. The 10-Year is near 5.10%.

feature_image.alt: Line chart, average retail diesel price per gallon, weekly, Jan. 5 to Nov. 16, 2026: the U.S. average rose from $3.48 to a record $6.53 on Sept. 21 and was $5.94 on Nov. 16; California rose to a record $8.25 the same week and was $7.73 on Nov. 16.
feature_image.caption: Diesel is under $6 nationally for the first time since early September; California pays about $1.80 more.
feature_image.source: U.S. Energy Information Administration, weekly retail diesel prices, through Nov. 16, 2026
